notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2022, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2022 is the latest available.
County school systems are part of county government in Tennessee, so school spending is included (it is left out of the services and overhead shares).
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($239,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Tennessee county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Tennessee yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Dyer County Sheriff's Office operates two Flock Safety automated license plate readers as of September 2025.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS016779, citing Public Records From the EFF via Pittsboro Police - See note

redFlags.label: Third-party investigative platform
redFlags.detail: The Dyer County Sheriff's Office has access to SoundThinking's CrimeTracer (formerly Coplink X) investigative platform through a statewide contract announced in April 2021.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012406, citing PR News Wire

redFlags.unscoredReason: Not scored: every police department in the state has this through a statewide contract, so it is not a local decision.

redFlags.label: Predictive policing
redFlags.detail: The Dyer County Sheriff's Office has access to a predictive analytics system developed by IBM to identify locations where vehicle crashes and DUIs are likely to occur. All 95 county sheriffs in the state access the system, which is managed by the Tennessee Highway Patrol.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS007070, citing Tennessee Department of Safety and Homeland Security

The Census surveys every government only in Census of Governments years (2022) and a sample in other years, so FY 2023 is the latest available.
Some Tennessee cities run their own school systems; where this one does, school spending is included and left out of the services and overhead shares. Residents also pay Dyer County.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Tennessee city candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Cameras: 11 license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Dyersburg's borders in OpenStreetMap (6 made by Flock Safety), not counting cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies. Flock cameras count as a red flag whoever runs them. Other brands count only when the government is the recorded operator, since many have no operator recorded.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-20. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals and corporate tax breaks have not been checked for Tennessee yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: Flock camera network
redFlags.detail: 6 Flock Safety license-plate cameras are mapped inside City of Dyersburg's borders in OpenStreetMap. Flock cameras photograph every passing car and feed a search network shared with police agencies across the country. Who runs each camera is recorded for some; cameras tagged as run by stores, malls, schools or state and regional agencies are not counted.
